## Objective
- Build a complete, playable Dreamcore exploration game focused on freely exploring a very large place, with lightweight realistic shaders, physics, wind, sanity, and an FPS display.

## Requirements
- No objective beyond exploration; make reasonable assumptions without asking questions.
- Use Indonesian interface text and support desktop and mobile controls.

## Decisions
- Game title: “Somewhere, Still”; browser-based Three.js first-person walking simulator.
- Include atmospheric landmarks, contextual interactions, wind/audio, sanity changes, and pause/resume.

## Work State
### Completed
- `index.html` and `style.css` provide the game UI, start/pause screens, HUD, FPS counter, sanity meter, and responsive controls.
- `game.js` has Three.js scene setup, terrain and sky shaders, instanced wind-bent grass, trees, and landmark-building functions/calls.
- A grass shader include was adjusted to use separate lines.

### Active
- Finish gameplay implementation in `game.js`: input, movement/physics, interaction, sanity, audio/wind, HUD, pause, resize, and render loop.
- Verify shader rendering and overall gameplay in a browser.

### Blocked
- Browser testing is pending; Playwright’s default Chromium was unavailable, though `playwright-cli --browser chrome open http://localhost:3002` worked previously.
- An earlier Playwright run on a superseded `game.js` reported `TypeError: clock.getDelta is not a function`; the latest rewrite declares `clock` as a `THREE.Clock`, but this remains unverified.

## Next Move
1. Inspect the current `game.js` and complete the missing runtime/gameplay code.
2. Run `node --check game.js` after the latest edits.
3. Test at `http://localhost:3002`; resolve console/shader errors and verify controls, FPS, sanity, wind, landmarks, and pause.
4. Capture and inspect a small JPEG screenshot.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: active Three.js implementation; gameplay and browser verification remain.
- `index.html`: game UI, HUD, and control elements.
- `style.css`: Dreamcore visual styling and responsive layouts.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted.
- A local server was started with `python3 -m http.server 3002`.
- The earlier clock error came from an older version; do not assume it persists or is resolved until testing the current file.
